title: Memory leak in OPCUA_MGR::initialize() (34 allocations, 385 bytes, every -d OPCUA_DEV startup)

events.body_markdown:
## Summary
Starting FORTE with the `-d OPCUA_DEV` device (see `doc/tutorials/opcuadeployment.adoc`) leaks 385 bytes across 34 allocations, every single time, confirmed via AddressSanitizer/LeakSanitizer. The leak originates from `OPCUA_MGR::initialize()` (called once, from `OPCUA_DEV::startDevice()`), via two sub-paths that both end up copying a `UA_NodeId`/`UA_String` into open62541's node store without that copy ever being freed:

- `OPCUA_MGR::addMethodNode()` — called once per management method OPCUA_MGR registers (`writeDevice`, `startDevice`, `stopDevice`, `resetDevice`, `killDevice`, per-resource/FB CRUD methods, etc.) — 31 of the 34 leaked allocations.
- `OPCUA_MGR::addMgmtObjectInstance()` — 3 of the 34 leaked allocations, for the management object instance node itself.

## Root cause (as far as traced)
Both paths eventually call into open62541's `addNode_raw()`/`Operation_addNode_begin()`, which internally does `UA_copy()` → `NodeId_copy()` → `String_copy()` → `UA_Array_copy()` to store its own copy of the requested `UA_NodeId`'s string component. That copy is what LeakSanitizer reports as never freed. I have not tracked down why this particular copy escapes cleanup (whether it's an OPCUA_MGR-side issue, e.g. never deleting these specific nodes before the server itself is torn down, or something open62541-side) -- flagging with the confirmed call sites and stack traces rather than guessing further.

## Reproduction
Build with `-DFORTE_COM_OPC_UA=ON -DFORTE_SYSTEM_TESTS=ON` and Address/LeakSanitizer enabled (e.g. via `-DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS=-fsanitize=address`), then run any bootfile with `-d OPCUA_DEV`:

```
./forte_systemtest -d OPCUA_DEV -f <any .fboot>
```

LeakSanitizer reports the leak at process exit regardless of which bootfile is used, since the leak happens during `OPCUA_DEV::startDevice()`, before any bootfile is even loaded.

## Evidence
Two representative stack traces (`ASAN_OPTIONS=fast_unwind_on_malloc=0:malloc_context_size=30`, needed because the default fast unwinder only resolves 2 frames on this build):

```
Direct leak of 20 byte(s) in 1 object(s) allocated from:
    #0 calloc
    #1 UA_Array_copy                 open62541/src/ua_types.c:2724
    #2 String_copy                   open62541/src/ua_types.c:288
    #3 NodeId_copy                   open62541/src/ua_types.c:799
    #4 UA_copy                       open62541/src/ua_types.c:2104
    #5 zipNsInsertNode               open62541/.../types_generated.h:584
    #6 addNode_raw                   open62541/src/server/ua_services_nodemanagement.c:1390
    #7 Operation_addNode_begin       open62541/src/server/ua_services_nodemanagement.c:1496
    #8 addMethodNode                 (open62541, constprop)
    #9 UA_Server_addMethodNode       open62541/src/server/ua_services_nodemanagement.c:3355
    #10 forte::iec61499::system::OPCUA_MGR::addMethodNode(...)           stdfblib/system/src/OPCUA_MGR.cpp:1578
    #11 forte::iec61499::system::OPCUA_MGR::addQueryGlobalConstTypeMethod(UA_Server*)  stdfblib/system/src/OPCUA_MGR.cpp:1345
    #12 forte::iec61499::system::OPCUA_MGR::createIEC61499MgmtObject(UA_Server*)       stdfblib/system/src/OPCUA_MGR.cpp:438
    #13 forte::iec61499::system::OPCUA_MGR::initialize()                              stdfblib/system/src/OPCUA_MGR.cpp:391
    #14 forte::iec61499::system::OPCUA_DEV::startDevice()                             stdfblib/system/src/OPCUA_DEV.cpp:30
    #15 forte::C4diacFORTEInstance::startupNewDevice(std::string const&)              core/src/forteinstance.cpp:36

```

```
Direct leak of ... byte(s) in ... object(s) allocated from:
    #0 calloc
    #1 UA_Array_copy ... (same chain as above)
    #10 forte::iec61499::system::OPCUA_MGR::addMgmtObjectInstance()   stdfblib/system/src/OPCUA_MGR.cpp:467
    #11 forte::iec61499::system::OPCUA_MGR::createIEC61499MgmtObject(UA_Server*)  stdfblib/system/src/OPCUA_MGR.cpp:444
    #12 forte::iec61499::system::OPCUA_MGR::initialize()                          stdfblib/system/src/OPCUA_MGR.cpp:391
```

`SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: 385 byte(s) leaked in 34 allocation(s).` -- consistently reproducible, not flaky.

## Environment
Found while building a systemtest for a different issue (#1053) that happens to use `-d OPCUA_DEV`; no other existing systemtest uses that device, which is presumably why this hasn't been caught before. POSIX/Linux build, `open62541` 1.5.8, ASan/LSan enabled build.

Fix proposed against a fork for now: https://github.com/Meisterschulen-am-Ostbahnhof-Munchen/4diac-forte/pull/59

Root cause confirmed: `UA_Server_addMethodNode()`/`UA_Server_addObjectNode()`'s `outNewNodeId` output parameter is caller-owned and must be released (per open62541's own docs), and `OPCUA_MGR` never did. Fixed by clearing the local NodeId in `addMethodNode()` right after use, and clearing `mMgmtTypeId`/`mMgmtNodeId`/`mResourceTypeId` in the destructor. Confirmed via LeakSanitizer: 385 bytes across 34 allocations before the fix, zero after.
